messages.author: e4fa8ed2dc96fc64
messages.subject: Generating plots with rapache
parts:
Hello!

First of all, contratulations for everyone! RApache is awsome! Never
thought R requests could be so fast and clean.

I'm facing some difficulties in generating plots through rapache. I
made some searches in this group, and for what I could read, it seems
it's a permission issue. It looks like some people presented some
solution, but, being honest, I couldn't understand it. I'm not a linux
experienced user, neither an apache expert, so maybe this problem is
solved, but the solution isn't clear for me.

After all, how did you get around this problem?

Cheers,

- Joao Daniel

messages.author: e4fa8ed2dc96fc64
messages.subject: Re: Generating plots with rapache
parts:
I was able to generate plots chmoding 777 /var/www folder. It makes
plots generation possible, but also generates a security flaw.

Is there any other approach?

Cheers!

- Joao Daniel

messages.author: 42eed4e1caba0ad0
messages.subject: Re: Generating plots with rapache
parts:
Well, I created a group called webdev, added user nobody to it with "sudo gpasswd -a nobody webdev", then "chown -R /var/www/* webdev", and "chmod -R 775 /var/www/*"... but that's just for development purposes (and I use ArchLinux, but that's irrelevant @ this point...).

But you don't need 777, you can use 765, since you don't need to execute image files! =)

parts:
Whaaa? O_o Could you mail me the response body from Net panel? Univar-plot requires stats, graphics and RJSONIO packages (sorry for omiting that one, and thanks for spotting an error).
Anyway, there's a strange behaviour (bug?) in RApache. You have to set:

REvalOnStartup "library(RJSONIO);"

in your main Apache conf, otherwise it won't load the package, which kind of sucks, since you'd probably like to keep everything in local .htaccess

Anyway, install RJSONIO package (available on CRAN), and put this line in your Apache conf (or just append "library(RJSONIO);" to existing line), and please try again. Be sure to flush your cache if you're using firefox, or just watch the response code (if 304, flush it)!

Thank you for kind words 'bout the design, and thanks again for spotting an error! =]

messages.subject: Re: Generating plots with rapache
parts:
I should mail Jeff, about this one. It looks like a bug to me. You should put:

REvalOnStartup "library(RJSONIO)"

in your global conf file (yup, the big one),

while leaving the <FilesMatch> stuff in local (.htaccess) file. Anyway, I think it's inappropriate to discuss my webapp through RApache mailing list. Mail me if you have problems with univar-plot. I appreciate that.

Anyway... about producing graphs with RApache... the trick is not to let brew::brew to evaluate all files in a directory, unless you have bunch of R scripts that rely on brew conventions in the same folder. Otherwise, you'll get an error, because brew will try to parse png files. Try to write a simple script:

png("foo.png")
plot(rnorm(100))
dev.off()

Run it through RApache and watch the headers. If it's not generating the code, try to figure out what's going wrong. If you're familiar with AJAX, attach it to html file and use some JS to grab the file path (in that case you should return a string - path to png). That's pretty much the main idea behind univar-plot. I never intended to write such application in the first place - I was just playing around with RApache and jQuery AJAX functions. So... I recommend you to do a small-scale test first. And watch the headers, especially the response body. Nothing more, nothing less...
